root_cause.text: In `mm/shmem.c`’s truncate path, `shmem_undo_range()` retried a failed `shmem_free_swap()` lookup using the same `index` even when the found large swap entry’s base index was below that index, causing `find_get_entries()` to return the same misaligned large swap entry repeatedly and spin forever.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes that when `index` points into the middle of a large swap entry, `shmem_free_swap()` fails because the entry’s “base < index”, then `shmem_confirm_swap()` confirms the same order and the code “retry with the same index,” leading to “an infinite loop”; the fix changes this to `index = base` after `round_down(base, 1 << order)` and aborts if the rounded base is outside the truncate range.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix shmem truncate undo logic to correctly handle large swap entries crossing either range boundary by retrying from the aligned base and skipping out-of-range clusters.
intent_record.what: In shmem_undo_range(), the code handling a failed shmem_free_swap() call was changed to introduce a local pgoff_t base initialized from indices[i], compute the swap order with shmem_confirm_swap(), and for large swap entries round base down to the swap cluster boundary. The border check was expanded from only testing whether the entry extends past end to also test whether it starts before start. The retry index assignment was changed from index = indices[i] to index = base, and the comment was updated to mention both start and end borders and that the swap may have been replaced by a page or extended.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes truncate/undo-range handling more accurate for large swap entries that overlap the truncation range boundary on either side. Such entries are now skipped if they extend outside the affected range at the start or end, and if they are still valid within the range the retry restarts from the aligned swap cluster base rather than the original page index. This prevents incorrect reprocessing of partially covered large swap entries and improves handling when swap entries have been replaced or expanded.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the truncate retry loop reusing the same index after a failed swap-entry lookup, which could spin on a misaligned large swap entry. In this snippet, the old helper `shmem_free_swap(mapping, indices[i], folio)` has been replaced with a bounded version `shmem_free_swap(mapping, indices[i], end - 1, folio)` that checks alignment and range before removing the swap entry: `base = round_down(xas.xa_index, nr_pages); if (base < index || base + nr_pages - 1 > end) nr_pages = 0; else xas_store(&xas, NULL);`.
